_provenance: M9 inter-organ coordination atlas (v1.10: 12 central-brain organs). EVERY gamma is extracted VERBATIM (read-only, never fitted) by the SantaLucia 1998 nearest-neighbour stacking metric (gamma = -mean(NN stacking dG37)) over each master gene's promoter window [TSS-2000, TSS+500] (2501 bp, coding strand) from NCBI RefSeq (GRCh38) -- the SAME read-only metric used by the DNA volume, the neuro chain, and mind M0. The 8 cortico-subcortical organs were frozen in v1.9 (gamma cited verbatim from the neuro package master-gene data files repro/neuro/_engine/data/{sensory_organ_gamma.json, spinal_master_genes.json}; GSX2/PHOX2B fetched this project by the same eutils/SantaLucia pipeline). v1.10 PROMOTES four further central organs whose gamma was fetched by THIS package's own pipeline (repro/mind/13-em-coordination/{extra_masters.json, fetch_extra_masters.py}): pallidum/NKX2-1 and forebrain_gaba_in/DLX2 (validated in v1.9's additive M9-EXT scale-sweep), plus basal_forebrain_chol/LHX8 and olfactory_bulb/PAX6 (added in v1.10, promoter sha256 recorded in extra_masters.json). corr(gamma, GC) = 0.9954 across these 12 regions, consistent with the wider atlas (0.994-0.995). The gamma layer is Layer-1 [F]. f0_hz is the region's empirically-dominant oscillation band: its BAND IDENTITY is cited to the experimental literature, but the absolute centre frequency in Hz is Layer-2 [O] (a representative value, NOT read from the gamma window and NOT tuned to any model target). neuro single-source reference: neuro v1.10.1.
_metric: gamma = mean(-NN dG37), SantaLucia 1998 (read-only; identical to DNA/neuro/M0)
_grading: gamma [F measured input]; band identity [cited]; absolute f0 in Hz [O representative]; ring geometry & R_brain [O]; ephaptic coupling kappa is a MEASURED fraction (neuro 19), not tuned.
_relation_to_M0: M0 emerges 4 organs (cerebrum/cerebellum/hypothalamus/hippocampus) and freezes their order/geometry (UNCHANGED in v1.10). M9 EXTENDS that measured set to the full central-brain loop and adds the inter-organ ephaptic coordination layer. The 4 M0 masters reappear here with byte-identical gamma (FOXG1->neocortex, EN1->cerebellum, SIM1->hypothalamus, LHX2->hippocampus); v1.9 added the thalamus, striatum, midbrain, brainstem of the canonical loop; v1.10 adds the pallidum, forebrain GABAergic interneuron hub, basal-forebrain cholinergic nucleus, and olfactory bulb.
_remaining_open: Toward 100% brain organs, three central regions (amygdala, septum, preoptic area) remain outside the atlas. As of v1.12 they are no longer an UN-examined 'tbd': they were checked against the PRIMARY developmental-neuroscience literature and confirmed to GENUINELY lack a single unambiguous canonical master TF (amygdala = multi-origin complex: ISL1/vLGE, PAX6/dLGE, DLX5 striatal, OTP/LHX-family/EBF3/DBX1 in the medial part; septum = ZIC1-5 redundant & not septum-specific; preoptic area = shares NKX2-1 with pallidum/hypothalamus, so an entry would double-count one promoter, and is itself an internally parcellated niche). Selecting any single master would be the over-claim the no-tuning rule forbids, so they are kept open ON PURPOSE. Full evidence with sources: data/brain_region_master_survey.json. Data-gate (b) therefore stands open as a documented HARD BIOLOGICAL LIMIT (not a closeable in-package gap): closing it needs future field consensus naming a single master, or a deliberate switch to subnucleus granularity -- neither available, neither a tuned constant. Data-gate (c) -- sensory<->central coupling -- is CLOSED (v1.11): nine sensory modalities enter mind BY VERBATIM CITATION from neuro v1.10.1 as the eight-node sensory_input_atlas.json, coupled to their anatomical central relays at the measured kappa in engine module M10 (chapter 14). Whether cognition functionally USES either coupling stays open (medium_efficacy_tested=0).
